title: refactor(ci): modernize build matrix, improve cache parallelism, bump actions and deps
author: Nina Patel
release_notes: - CI: unify and simplify build/test workflows across repos; - Performance: parallelize cache uploads and reduce redundant matrix jobs; - Build tooling: bump actions and node versions; - Hygiene: remove legacy workflow variants
description: Context: our GitHub Actions workflows have accumulated ad-hoc matrix entries, duplicated steps across repo types, and stale action versions. This causes long queue times, inconsistent cache behaviour, and frequent CI failures after infra updates. Motivation: reduce CI wall-clock time, improve cache hit stability, simplify maintenance surface, and bring actions/node versions up-to-date for security and speed. What this PR does: 1) Consolidates lint/test/release workflows into a shared top-level workflow where possible while keeping repo-specific jobs small. 2) Reduces build matrix cardinality by moving platform-specific tests into targeted jobs and introducing feature flags for optional matrix axes. 3) Improves cache parallelism and upload ordering to avoid cache stampedes on large matrices. 4) Bumps GitHub Actions usages (actions/checkout, actions/setup-node, cache actions) to the latest vetted minor versions and pins hashes where appropriate. 5) Standardizes Node versions across workflows (16 -> 18 in helpers, 18 -> 20 for build/test where supported) and adds compatibility guards. 6) Removes legacy workflow files used by the old release pipeline and migrates release automation to the consolidated workflow with improved tagging/notes steps. Checklist: - [x] Consolidate workflows into .github/workflows/ci.yml and .github/workflows/release.yml - [x] Reduce matrix size for packages and packages/cli - [x] Implement deterministic cache keys and parallel upload steps - [x] Bump actions/setup-node and actions/cache usages and pin hashes - [x] Validate on redwood, redwood-sdk-python, redwood-helm-charts via canary runs - [x] Add migration notes for devs and update CONTRIBUTING.md Testing & validation: ran the full matrix on redwood (canary run) and observed ~35% reduction in total CI runtime and 4x reduction in peak concurrent runners for larger jobs. Verified cache hit rates improved on subsequent runs. Also validated release job dry-runs for tag generation and changelog extraction. Rollout: merged to main after approvals; kept legacy workflows disabled for two weeks before removal to allow quick rollback. Links: Linear ENG-1423 and ENG-2110 track the consolidation and cache work. Related PRs: refs refactor-ci-unify-workflows-2026 and several previous pipeline hygiene PRs. Implementation notes: the cache step now writes partial caches from grouped matrix shards and then a final aggregator job updates the single cache namespace so that subsequent builds hit the unified cache. We added a small jitter to upload timings and split large workspace paths to avoid single large uploads that exceeded GitHub Actions timeouts. Backcompat: repository-specific overrides remain supported via workflow_dispatch inputs and matrix overrides. Please review the matrix reduction decisions in packages/ and packages/cli/OWNERS for risk areas.

review_comments: Samir Chaudhry: Can you call out which slow suites were kept in the matrix and why? We want to ensure no silent test coverage regressions.

Liam O'Connor: Suggestion: pin actions to full commit SHAs for the next release window to prevent surprise behaviour from minor releases.
